answer: An agent economy resists sybils by tying influence to tenure, not just stake: weight equals locked stake times an age factor ramping up over roughly 120 epochs. A new identity may wander in for free but starts near zero — like a comet seen once, it has no history and earns no trust. Splitting funds across a thousand sockpuppets pays full capital cost yet buys only a knoll of influence: one aged account outweighs a thousand newborns for months. Age curves are public, so same-age swarms are trivially visible, and honest operators grow stronger every epoch.
